chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever hankers after contraries gets no means of success.

key_terms.أَوْمَأَ: To gesture towards, indicate, or hanker after
key_terms.الْحِيَلُ: Means, methods, stratagems, or resources for success
key_terms.مُتَفَاوِتٍ: Contraries, differing things, or mutually exclusive items

ai.seo_question: What happens when a person desires contradictory things at the same time?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns that desiring mutually exclusive outcomes simultaneously leads to the failure of one's strategies (huyal), as the mind and efforts become divided. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of internal coherence (ittisāq) as a prerequisite for effective action, where conflicting desires create spiritual and practical disarray. The warning underscores the necessity of singular focus and clarity of purpose in both worldly endeavors and spiritual pursuit.
